A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQ-MANO and masked-transformer research, renamed from MMHMR to MaskHand. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results, architectural ablations, text-to-mesh generation and mesh-guided image-generation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction and generation results and adds DexYCB reconstruction, severe-masking tests, keypoint-source analysis and unconditional mesh generation.

M1.justification: The core tokenizer, masked transformer, losses and confidence-guided reconstruction procedure remain substantially unchanged. v2 adds an unconditional-generation adaptation using a zero image condition and Top-100 sampling, and removes the downstream ControlNet image-generation pipeline. The GAPR renaming and expanded GCN description do not establish a changed reconstruction algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds supervised reconstruction evaluation on DexYCB, previously used for training and image-generation experiments, and introduces HInt scenarios with 80% and 90% masked hand regions. It also adds unconditional mesh generation and removes mesh-guided hand-image generation. ASL text-to-mesh coverage already existed in v1.

E2.justification: The new DexYCB comparison includes previously unevaluated comparators such as MobRecon, H2ONet, Spurr et al. and Liu et al.; unconditional generation introduces a PCA baseline. The HaMeR comparison for ControlNet image generation disappears. Comparator membership in the retained HO3Dv3, FreiHAND and ordinary HInt comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include DexYCB-specific supervised evaluation with aligned and unaligned errors, 80%/90% image masking, ground-truth versus estimated keypoint controls, and 2,000 unconditional samples evaluated using APD and self-intersection. v2 also introduces inference-time measurement and removes the ControlNet FID-H, KID-H and detection-confidence evaluation. The stated FreiHAND-only training setup already existed in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled severe-occlusion tests, sensitivity to OpenPose versus ground-truth keypoints, and qualitative component ablations. It removes the quantitative token-rank sampling analysis, control-signal ablations, x-Attention-head ablation and 10-iteration result. Tokenizer, masking-range, loss, feature-scale and attention-depth analyses are largely retained through relocation.

E5.justification: The text-to-mesh means and standard deviations are identical in v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 6. Confidence visualizations already existed in v1. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new generation sample count is an evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: FreiHAND Table 2 changes PA-MPJPE/PA-MPVPE from 5.7/5.5 to 5.5/5.4 mm and F@5 from 0.793 to 0.801; iteration-study values also change. v2 adds DexYCB, severe-masking, keypoint-source, unconditional-generation and latency results, while removing image-generation and quantitative token-rank results. HO3Dv3 and ordinary HInt scores remain unchanged, and several appendix ablations retain the earlier FreiHAND values.

T1.justification: The quantization, graph-refinement, deformable-attention, masked-likelihood, expected-embedding, loss and camera-projection formulations are retained. Expanded architectural explanations introduce no substantive mathematical derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit introduction contribution claiming a generic framework that unifies hand-mesh estimation and generation. The central claims about generative masked reconstruction, confidence-guided sampling, robustness and state-of-the-art accuracy remain. Text-conditioned generation already supported a narrower version of the expanded positioning in v1.

C2.justification: v2 identifies keypoint-estimation accuracy as a constraint on reconstruction quality and interprets unconditional-generation results through PCA's linear-subspace restriction and confidence-based plausibility assessment. Interpretations concerning ControlNet guidance and the negligible benefit of 10 decoding iterations disappear. The main explanation linking confidence-guided reconstruction to occlusion robustness is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses 200K transformer-training iterations, explains fixed-skeleton GCN processing of OpenPose cues, and identifies the RTX A5000 used for timing. It removes the ControlNet training and caption-generation recipe. Most core optimizer, batch-size, loss-weight and tokenizer details remain unchanged; the newly disclosed training duration does not establish an increased budget.

R1.justification: Targeted citation additions include OpenPose, ViTDet, MobRecon, H2ONet and other DexYCB comparators. ControlNet, LLaVA-OneVision, Handiffuser and MediaPipe references disappear with the image-generation study. The related-work organization and central distinction from discriminative methods and HHMR remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming MMHMR and GGPM, v2 rewrites the method overview and experimental narrative and substantially reorganizes the document. Existing text-to-mesh material becomes Section 4.3, HInt all/visible-joint results and component/masking ablations move into the appendix, and appendix sections are reordered and consolidated.

P2.justification: Benchmark tables are reformatted, HInt results are split, architecture and text-to-mesh diagrams are relocated or redrawn, and masking, unconditional-generation and component-ablation figures are added. ControlNet figures disappear and the appendix changes to a single-column layout. v2 Figure 18 incorrectly redisplays Figure 17's attention visualization under an in-the-wild reconstruction caption.

improvement.justification: The controlled severe-occlusion tests, keypoint-sensitivity analysis and inference timings provide more direct support for the central robustness and practicality claims, alongside an additional reconstruction benchmark. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by removal of quantitative token-rank evidence, unexplained differences between updated main FreiHAND scores and retained ablation values, and the duplicated Figure 18. The core method and much of its supporting evidence were already established in v1.
